{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Moss Eisenberg Sweedler''' (born 29 April 1942, in [[Brooklyn]])<ref>Dates of birth, report from Guggenheim Foundation 1980</ref> is an American mathematician, known for [[Sweedler's Hopf algebra]], [[Coalgebra#Sweedler notation|Sweedler's notation]], [[measuring coalgebra]]s, and his proof, with Harry Prince Allen, of a conjecture of [[Nathan Jacobson]].

==Education and career==
Sweedler received his Ph.D. from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1965. His thesis, ''Commutative Hopf Algebras with Antipode,'' was written under the direction of thesis advisor [[Bertram Kostant]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=37235}}</ref> Sweedler wrote ''Hopf Algebras'' (1969), which became the standard reference book on [[Hopf algebra]]s. He, with Harry P. Allen, used Hopf algebras to prove in 1969 a famous 25-year-old conjecture of Jacobson about the forms of generalized Witt algebras over algebraically closed fields of finite characteristic. From 1965 to the mid 1980s Sweeder worked on commutative algebra and related disciplines.<ref name="SweedlerHomepage">[https://www.math.cornell.edu/m/People/Faculty/sweedler Moss E. Sweedler, www.math.cornell.edu]</ref> Since the mid 1980s Sweedler has worked primarily on [[computer algebra]]. His research resulted in his position as director of the [[Sustainment Center of Excellence|Army Center of Excellence]] for computer algebra.<ref name=SweedlerHomepage/>

Sweedler was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1974 in Vancouver.<ref>{{cite book|author=Sweedler, Moss Eisenberg|chapter-url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1974.1/Main/icm1974.1.0337.0342.ocr.pdf|chapter=Something like the Brauer group|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vancouver, 1974|pages=337–341}}</ref> He was a Guggenheim Fellow for the academic year 1980–1981.<ref>[http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/moss-e-sweedler/ John Simon Guggenheim Foundation | Moss E. Sweedler]</ref>

With his wife Kristin, he helped establish the Sweedler Nature Preserve.<ref>[https://www.visitithaca.com/attractions/lick-brook-falls-sweedler-nature-preserve/ Lick Brook Falls @ Sweedler Nature Preserve]</ref>
